amendments.rule: A target head is the cross-language lexical display anchor: the English token that most directly realizes the source head's lexeme, with English syntax used only to break a genuine tie. Do not choose a word merely because it is first, finite, or the phrase's formal syntactic head. Choose the lexical predicate over subjects and auxiliaries (`was given` heads on `given`), and the meaning-bearing complement in support/light-verb or resultative renderings (`make straight` heads on `straight`; `bear witness` on `witness`). When a substantival Greek adjective or demonstrative is expanded with a generic English noun, choose the adjective or demonstrative (`all things` heads on `All`; `good thing` on `good`). That clause is scoped to **anarthrous** Greek, where no article stands to take the supplied noun. Where a Greek article governs the phrase, rule 102 gives the article the supplied noun and leaves the adjective or demonstrative its own bare word, so no shared head is in question: `τὰ πάντα` → *all things* is the article's *things* and the quantifier's *all*, as `τὸ τρίτον` → *the third part* is under rule 49, and heading the whole phrase on *all* is the error rule 102 records JAS.1.11 correcting. When a case-inflected Greek article becomes `on the`, choose `the`; the preposition realizes case. For a source noun rendered by `of + noun`, choose the noun. Review this choice independently, and split separately recoverable names rather than assigning an arbitrary shared head.
amendments.why: Rule 17's `all things` heads on `All` is unqualified and is wrong for articular Greek, which rule 102 settled unanimously (fifty-three units to none, twelve to none for the substantival-adjective shape) and could only correct by cross-reference. This chapter met the case four times — τῶν πνευματικῶν at 12:1, τὰ πάντα at 12:6, τὰ ἀσχήμονα at 12:23 and τὰ εὐσχήμονα at 12:24 — and each verse had to argue against the sentence it was reading first. The amendment changes no outcome and adds no law: it moves rule 102's scoping into the rule whose example misleads, which is what rule 102's own closing sentence asks for. Nothing else in rule 17 is altered.

conventions: Supplied English connectives in this chapter divide by whether a source token licenses them. At an asyndetic seam between like members of the gift lists the ASV's *and* is `added` under rule 98 — once at 12:9 and four times at 12:10 — and where the ASV writes no juncture nothing is supplied, as before ἑτέρῳ at 12:10. Where an expressed conjunction governs two coordinate members and the ASV repeats its English, the repetition is a rule 7 helper on the member it introduces and is never `added`: 12:25's second *that* belongs to μεριμνῶσι, the ἵνα it repeats standing in the same sentence, which is rule 103's function-word contrast. A chapter writing both is not inconsistent.

1CO.12.26 carries a doubled ἕν. Unit SBLGNT.1CO.12.26.v022 selected r01, which supplies ἓν μέλος where the base writes μέλος alone in the second clause, and the projection places both numeral tokens in the first clause while the ASV writes *one* there and an italicized *one* in the second. The second token is aligned to the italicized *one*. Where a projection's token placement and the ASV's clause disagree but the lexeme and function match, pair them under rule 15; do not record the same word as surplus on both sides, since rule 97's mirror case wants source the ASV did not translate and rule 103's `added` wants a licensing token already spent.

Where a verbless clause's subject is a substantival quantifier or adjective rather than a pronoun, rule 63's pronoun exception does not reach it and the supplied copula is the predicate nominal's helper: 12:17 gives *were hearing* to ἀκοή under the subject ὅλον, and 12:29 gives *are apostles*, *are prophets*, *are teachers* and *are … miracles* to the predicate nouns under πάντες. Rule 68's demonstrative arm was not extended to a quantifier, its reason being that a demonstrative is no more a lexical noun than ὑμεῖς is, which would also carry to πάντες; the reading giving *are all* to the quantifier is therefore defensible and was not taken.

report: Cross-verse scan: all 44 candidate lemmas read, and no cross-verse split found. The differences the table shows are licensed by the ASV's own rendering or by a difference in the Greek.

Articles: articular substantival adjectives take the supplied nominal at 12:1 (gifts), 12:6 (things), 12:23 and 12:24 (parts) under rule 102, the adjective staying bare each time; second attributive articles are unrepresented at 12:2 and 12:31 alike; the article before theos/Christos is unrepresented at 12:12, 12:18, 12:24 and 12:28 because the ASV writes no determiner for it; an article governing an expressed head noun leaves the relativizer to its participle at 12:6 and 12:22, and the substantival article at 12:24 keeps only its supplied nominal and case preposition under rule 32.

Copulas run one way through the chapter: an expressed copula keeps its own subject (12:15, 12:16, 12:27); a supplied one is the predicate noun's helper where the subject is a noun, substantival adjective or quantifier (12:3, 12:17, 12:29); the predicate carries subject and copula together where no subject stands (12:20, rule 68); and the subject carries it where no predicate stands (12:12, rule 56).

Other recurring items checked and consistent: men unrepresented at 12:8, 12:20, 12:28 (rule 70); the kai of kai gar unrepresented at 12:13 and 12:14 (rule 65); kathos keeps 'even as' whole at 12:11 and 12:18, no kai answering it (rule 82); chreian echo split under rule 2 at 12:21 twice and 12:24; the preverb syn- rides inside its verb at 12:24 and twice at 12:26 (rule 106); pou carries the supplied copula at 12:17 twice and 12:19. hekasto to 'to each one' at 12:7 and 12:11 against hen hekaston to 'each one' at 12:18 is not a split: at 12:18 a source token stands for 'one' and takes it.

One real error, confined to 12:26: the same word was recorded as surplus on both sides. The projection's second hen (s005, from unit SBLGNT.1CO.12.26.v022's selected r01) was left unrepresented under rule 97's mirror case while the ASV's italicized 'one' (t013) was marked added under rule 103. Each status fails its own test - rule 97's mirror wants source the ASV did not translate, and the ASV writes 'one'; rule 103 wants a licensing token already spent, and s005 is wholly unspent. Patched to one aligned unit s005 -> t013, with the variant unit named in the note and the earlier reading conceded. The uncertainty is the projection's placement of the token in the first clause; rule 15 covers that, and rule 12 forbids re-deciding the text here.

BSB disagreements: none is an error. The unrepresented articular-construction article at 12:7 is rules 61 and 23; the unrepresented men at 12:20 and the seven interrogative me at 12:29-30 are cases where rules 70 and 44 say in terms that the report is not a correction; the unrepresented kath at 12:31 follows rule 94's own citation of GAL.1.13, the ASV having written two English words for kath' hyperbolen so that no compound unit is available and no English word answers to the preposition.

Recorded three conventions (supplied connectives, the doubled hen at 12:26, and the subject class that carries a supplied copula) and one amendment to rule 17, which leaves an over-broad example rule 102 has already corrected. No new rule: nothing else here generalises.
